issues.detail: The Hebrew 'לֹא יְשׁוּרֶנָּה' means 'he does not regard it' (i.e., God does not consider/observe it), but the Chinese renders it as '都不改變' (does not change), which changes the meaning. The subject of 'יְשׁוּרֶנָּה' is God, and the object is the matter spoken; the Chinese implies God's own unchangeableness, whereas the Hebrew says God does not look upon/regard the thing (or possibly 'he does not see it' in the sense of not repeating it). This is a substantive semantic shift.
